steps.what: Clarify laboratory service requests, specimen context and the information needed by referring professionals
Review laboratory findings and provide checked information with limitations to the referring professional

tasks.design: Retain service clarification and laboratory interpretation with the microbiologist using {TELEPHONY} and the laboratory information system {OTHER}. Native sample records support the service, while information used for diagnosis or public-health decisions needs professional interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service requests and findings require context-specific interpretation and direct clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory records support traceability without replacing the professional judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Specimen limitations or contamination can change the meaning of an apparently clear result.
tasks.human_edge: The microbiologist recognises uncertainty and communicates consequences and limitations.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in service interpretation or change in clinical authority.

reach.learn: Communicate analytical limitations without taking over clinical diagnosis.

evidence.claim: SciSure supports laboratory sample tracking and workflows; this does not demonstrate diagnostic interpretation capability.

assumptions: Boundary is service scoping and professional interpretation. Physical assays and microscopy belong to their specific tasks and must not be added again at team roll-up.

Laboratory staff produce findings and quality-control records during separately scoped assay execution, before s2; the microbiologist checks their meaning here. No automated result-validity or diagnosis flag is assumed.
OTHER means laboratory information system. Consider native records first. Zero upkeep because no new tool or workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Current result handling and quality controls
research_questions: Which missing specimen details most often alter the interpretation or require clarification?

already_counted.description: All service clarification, interpretation and checked communication remain counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact findings, specimen context, interpretation and limitations; changes require new authorisation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Professional service interpretation remains unchanged; separately scoped assays earn no duplicate saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test environmental and food specimens for microorganisms

steps.what: Monitor sampling conditions and perform microbiological tests on water, food and environmental specimens
Interpret tests for harmful microorganisms and investigate possible contamination or infection sources

tasks.design: Retain specimen testing and microbiological assessment with the microbiologist, with methods and observations in {DOCS}. Existing laboratory instruments assist procedures; no new automated test interpretation is established here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sampling representativeness and organism detection require method-specific physical work and interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing test methods and records support reliable execution without eliminating it.
tasks.still_hard: Negative findings can reflect sampling or method limits rather than absence of contamination.
tasks.human_edge: The microbiologist evaluates controls and distinguishes evidence of contamination from uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in testing or source investigation.

reach.learn: Relate laboratory observations to sampling conditions and exposure pathways.

evidence.claim: Retaining physical microbiological testing and interpretation is model knowledge; no task-specific saving is demonstrated.

assumptions: Boundary is environmental and food test execution and technical assessment; client service communication and separately listed microscopy are excluded from this baseline.
Microbiologist produces test and control observations during s1; no free positive/negative, validity or source-attribution flag is assumed.
Native instrument functions are considered first; existing unattended incubation or instrument runtime is not human labour. Zero added upkeep because no change is proposed.
unknowns: Test methods and current instrument automation
research_questions: Which inconclusive results require repeat sampling rather than stronger interpretation?

already_counted.description: Testing, control evaluation and technical interpretation remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Physical procedures and scientific interpretation remain intact; instrument runtime earns no labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Examine physiological, morphological and cultural characteristics to identify and classify microorganisms

tasks.design: Retain microscopy and organism classification with the microbiologist using the microscope workstation {OTHER}. Reference material supports identification, while ambiguous morphology and mixed specimens require professional judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specimen quality, mixed organisms and uncommon features limit fixed-rule identification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing imaging aids support observation without establishing autonomous classification here.
tasks.still_hard: Visual similarity does not always establish species or clinical significance.
tasks.human_edge: The microbiologist recognises ambiguity and chooses confirmatory investigation.
tasks.altitude: Microscopic examination and classification responsibility are unchanged.

reach.learn: Connect preparation artifacts to classification uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Retaining microscopy-based organism classification is model knowledge; the digest does not establish an applicable image classifier.

assumptions: Boundary is examination and identification from prepared specimens; preparation and broader assay execution are separately scoped and unchanged.
OTHER means microscope workstation. Microbiologist produces observations and uncertainty within s1; no structured morphology or classification flag is assumed in advance.
Consider existing native imaging aids first. Zero upkeep because no new automation or capture process is introduced.
research_questions: Which ambiguous observations require a different method rather than further image inspection?

already_counted.description: Observation, classification and uncertainty assessment remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Microscopy remains fully human with no assumed automated classification gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Supervise technologists, technicians and scientists through work direction, observation, coaching and issue resolution

tasks.design: Keep scientific supervision, coaching and practical direction with the microbiologist, using {DOCS} for existing procedures. Sample tracking software does not replace assessment of staff practice and laboratory issues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision depends on direct observation, trust and scientific context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing procedures support consistent guidance without removing the supervisory relationship.
tasks.still_hard: A recorded completion can conceal misunderstanding or unsafe practice.
tasks.human_edge: The microbiologist recognises when a person needs help and provides specific feedback.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in supervision time or personnel rights.

reach.learn: Translate observed capability gaps into practical development needs.

evidence.claim: Scientific coaching and supervisory judgement remain human work, based on model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is direct supervision; staff execution and separately scoped testing remain outside this task.
Microbiologist observes practice and produces guidance during s1; no free structured staff-performance score is assumed.
Consider existing native procedure access first. Zero upkeep because no model, staff scoring or new workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which laboratory issues require direct observation rather than record-based supervision?

already_counted.description: All practical supervision, coaching and issue resolution remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Direct scientific supervision remains unchanged without invented scheduling or reporting work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical testing, organism identification, service interpretation and staff supervision remain central to the role.
reach: Connect laboratory uncertainty to referrer needs and practical staff development.
role.ambitious_version: A microbiologist who makes uncertainty clear and strengthens laboratory practice through direct evidence and coaching.
